abstract: The role of postoperative enteral immunonutrition (Post-IN) after pancreatoduodenectomy (PD) remains controversial. This study evaluated its association with postoperative outcomes. A retrospective multicenter study including 204 patients undergoing PD between 2017 and 2025 was performed. Patients receiving Post-IN were compared with those receiving standard postoperative nutritional care. Propensity Score Matching with a 1:1 ratio was used to reduce selection bias. Primary endpoints included 90-day mortality, failure-to-rescue (FTR), morbidity, and pancreas-specific complications. Propensity score matching generated two balanced groups of 51 patients each. After matching, Post-IN was associated with significantly lower 90-day mortality (OR < 0.01, 95% CI < 0.01-0.49; p = 0.013) and FTR (OR < 0.01, 95% CI < 0.01-0.30; p = 0.002). Rates of POPF, clinically relevant POPF, delayed gastric emptying, post-pancreatectomy hemorrhage, biliary leakage, major morbidity, reoperation, and length of hospital stay were comparable between two groups. CCI was lower in the Post-IN group, although the difference did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.061). On multivariable Firth logistic regression, Post-IN remained independently associated with reduced 90-day mortality and FTR. Post-IN was associated with reduced mortality and FTR without affecting the incidence of pancreas-specific complications. These findings support the hypothesis that immunonutrition may enhance the patient's response to postoperative complications rather than preventing their occurrence. However, well powered randomized controlled trials are needed.

title: Postoperative immunonutrition following pancreatoduodenectomy mitigates the consequences of postoperative complications: a propensity score-matched analysis
